---
title: Component Tokens
description: The component-scoped custom properties a Visor theme can bind for the admin-UI families — table, chip, filter bar, page header, empty state, banner, sidebar, tabs, skeleton, spinner — each with a documented Tier-1 fallback.
---

A Visor theme has always been able to repaint the Tier-1 semantic surface —
`--surface-*`, `--text-*`, `--border-*`, `--interactive-*`. That is enough to make
an admin UI *functional*. It is not enough to make it look like **one thing**:
nothing stopped a page inventing its own table-header treatment, its own chip
tracking, its own filter-bar padding. A fidelity retro on a shipped admin app
measured the result — 247 element categories across 13 families whose
inconsistency traced to the substrate, not to any one component. The page title
rendered five ways; the table header cell four ways; the same mono status chip at
8.5 / 9 / 9.5 / 10 / 11px across nine implementations.

**Component tokens close that gap.** Each family below exposes a set of
component-scoped custom properties a theme binds once, in its `.visor.yaml`.
Distil the design into the theme, and every consuming surface inherits it —
instead of each page re-deriving the look in local CSS.

## The two guarantees

1. **Bind nothing and nothing changes.** Every token is read as
   `var(--token, <Tier-1 expression>)` where the fallback is byte-for-byte what
   the component rendered before the token existed. A theme with no
   `components:` block is pixel-identical to a theme from before this contract,
   and the engine emits no extra CSS at all.
2. **Bind one thing and every surface follows.** A bound token retunes every
   consuming rule at once — the whole point of moving the decision into the
   theme.

## Binding a family

```yaml
# my-theme.visor.yaml
components:
  table:
    head-height: "2.5rem"
    head-font-family: '"IBM Plex Mono", monospace'
    head-font-size: "11px"
    head-text-transform: uppercase
    head-letter-spacing: "0.06em"
    head-bg:
      light: "#f7f7f8"
      dark: "#141418"
  chip:
    md-font-size: "11px"
    letter-spacing: "0.04em"
    text-transform: uppercase
  badge:
    text-transform: uppercase
    letter-spacing: "0.04em"
    font-size: "11px"
    font-weight: "600"
```

A bare string binds both modes; `{ light, dark }` binds them independently, and a
binding may be mode-asymmetric (dark only, say). Family and key names are
validated — an unknown key is an **error**, not a warning, because a typo'd
component token is otherwise silently inert: the component just keeps resolving
its fallback and you never learn the binding missed.

## Where the CSS lands

Bound tokens emit into the `visor-adaptive` cascade layer, on the same selectors
as the Tier-1 adaptive set (light on the host selector; dark on the manual-toggle
selectors plus a `prefers-color-scheme` query). Single-mode brands
(`color-scheme: dark-only` / `light-only`) collapse onto the host selector, with
no toggle blocks — the same shape every other emitter uses.

Component `.module.css` files use no `@layer` at all, so a consumer that really
must override one surface locally still can. The point of this contract is that
they should not have to.

## Overriding without a theme

The same properties work as plain CSS custom properties, so a block or a page
shell can scope a treatment without touching the theme:

```css
.myAdminShell {
  --table-head-text-transform: uppercase;
  --table-head-letter-spacing: 0.06em;
}
```

Prefer the theme. A local override is exactly the per-page divergence this
contract exists to end — reach for it only when the treatment genuinely belongs
to one surface.

## The contract


### `table`

Table head, row and cell treatment. The retro measured the same header cell rendered four ways across one admin app; binding this family pins it once.

| Token | Binds | Falls back to |
|---|---|---|
| `--table-font-size` | Base table type size. | `var(--font-size-sm, 0.875rem)` |
| `--table-text-color` | Base table text colour. | `var(--text-primary, #111827)` |
| `--table-head-height` | Header row height. | `3rem` |
| `--table-head-padding-x` | Header cell horizontal padding. | `var(--spacing-3, 0.75rem)` |
| `--table-head-font-family` | Header cell family — set a mono/condensed face for a chrome-style header. | `inherit` |
| `--table-head-font-size` | Header cell type size. | `inherit` |
| `--table-head-font-weight` | Header cell weight. | `var(--font-weight-medium, 500)` |
| `--table-head-letter-spacing` | Header cell tracking. | `inherit` |
| `--table-head-text-transform` | Header cell casing — `uppercase` for the editorial admin header. | `inherit` |
| `--table-head-color` | Header cell text colour. | `var(--text-primary, #111827)` |
| `--table-head-bg` | Header cell fill. Sits above the shared `--dt-header-bg` surface role. | `var(--dt-header-bg, transparent)` |
| `--table-row-border` | Row separator (width, style and colour). | `1px solid var(--border-default, #e5e7eb)` |
| `--table-row-hover-bg` | Row hover fill. | `var(--surface-muted, #f3f4f6)` |
| `--table-row-selected-bg` | Selected-row fill. | `var(--surface-muted, #f3f4f6)` |
| `--table-cell-padding` | Body cell padding. | `var(--spacing-3, 0.75rem)` |
| `--table-cell-font-size` | Body cell type size. | `inherit` |
| `--table-cell-color` | Body cell text colour. | `var(--text-primary, #111827)` |
| `--table-cell-bg` | Body cell fill. Sits above the shared `--dt-row-bg` surface role. | `var(--dt-row-bg, transparent)` |
| `--table-cell-border-top` | Cell hairline. | `var(--hairline-width, 1px) solid var(--hairline, transparent)` |
| `--table-footer-bg` | Footer row fill. | `var(--surface-muted, #f3f4f6)` |
| `--table-caption-color` | Caption text colour. | `var(--text-secondary, #6b7280)` |

### `data-table`

The admin-ui Tier-2 data-table surface stack (D3). Shared between the Table primitive and the DataTable shell so a list page and its table read as one surface.

| Token | Binds | Falls back to |
|---|---|---|
| `--dt-header-bg` | Header-row surface tier. | `transparent` |
| `--dt-row-bg` | Data-row surface tier — a hair above the page so rows track any palette. | `transparent` |
| `--dt-container-radius` | Table container rounding — `0` lets the consumer shell own the corners. | `var(--radius-lg, 0.5rem)` |
| `--dt-container-shadow` | Table container elevation. | `var(--shadow-sm)` |
| `--dt-row-py` | Row vertical rhythm (the density axis). | `var(--spacing-3, 0.75rem)` |
| `--dt-cell-px` | Cell horizontal inset. | `var(--spacing-5, 1.25rem)` |
| `--dt-header-font-size` | Sort-header type size. | `11px` |

### `chip`

Chip / filter-pill treatment. The retro found the same mono status chip at 8.5 / 9 / 9.5 / 10 / 11px with tracking .03–.14em across nine implementations; this family is the single dial.

| Token | Binds | Falls back to |
|---|---|---|
| `--chip-radius` | Chip corner rounding. | `var(--radius-full, 9999px)` |
| `--chip-border` | Outlined-chip edge colour. Width and style come from the shared `control` edge, so `control.edge-width: 0` turns it off. | `var(--control-edge-color, var(--border-default, #e5e7eb))` |
| `--chip-bg` | Resting chip fill. | `var(--surface-card, #ffffff)` |
| `--chip-text-color` | Chip label colour. | `var(--text-primary, #111827)` |
| `--chip-font-family` | Chip label family — bind a mono face for token/ID chips. | `var(--font-body, inherit)` |
| `--chip-font-weight` | Chip label weight. | `var(--font-weight-medium, 500)` |
| `--chip-letter-spacing` | Chip label tracking. | `inherit` |
| `--chip-text-transform` | Chip label casing. | `inherit` |
| `--chip-sm-height` | Small chip height. | `1.5rem` |
| `--chip-sm-padding-x` | Small chip horizontal padding. | `var(--spacing-2, 0.5rem)` |
| `--chip-sm-font-size` | Small chip type size. | `var(--font-size-xs, 0.75rem)` |
| `--chip-md-height` | Default chip height. | `2rem` |
| `--chip-md-padding-x` | Default chip horizontal padding. | `var(--spacing-3, 0.75rem)` |
| `--chip-md-font-size` | Default chip type size. | `var(--font-size-sm, 0.875rem)` |
| `--chip-lg-height` | Large chip height. | `2.5rem` |
| `--chip-lg-padding-x` | Large chip horizontal padding. | `var(--spacing-4, 1rem)` |
| `--chip-lg-font-size` | Large chip type size. | `var(--font-size-base, 1rem)` |
| `--chip-selected-bg` | Selected chip fill. | `var(--surface-accent-subtle, #eff6ff)` |
| `--chip-selected-border-color` | Selected chip edge colour. | `var(--surface-accent-default, #3b82f6)` |
| `--chip-selected-text-color` | Selected chip label colour. | `var(--text-link, #2563eb)` |

### `badge`

Badge treatment — the D3 Tier-2 `--badge-text-transform` / `-letter-spacing` / `-font-size` / `-font-weight` set, promoted from the admin-ui audit to a bindable contract.

| Token | Binds | Falls back to |
|---|---|---|
| `--badge-radius` | Badge corner rounding. | `var(--radius-full, 9999px)` |
| `--badge-border` | Badge outline. | `1px solid transparent` |
| `--badge-font-family` | Badge label family. | `inherit` |
| `--badge-font-weight` | Badge label weight (Tier-2: 600). | `var(--font-weight-medium, 500)` |
| `--badge-text-transform` | Badge casing (Tier-2: uppercase). | `none` |
| `--badge-letter-spacing` | Badge tracking (Tier-2: 0.04em). | `normal` |
| `--badge-font-size` | Default badge type size (Tier-2: 11px). Drives both the standard and editorial-density steps. | `var(--font-size-xs, 0.75rem)` |
| `--badge-md-padding` | Default badge padding. | `calc(var(--spacing-1, 0.25rem) / 2) var(--spacing-2, 0.5rem)` |
| `--badge-md-gap` | Default badge icon gap. | `var(--spacing-1, 0.25rem)` |
| `--badge-bg` | Badge ground in every variant (an accent tint, an on-image scrim). Unset, each variant keeps its own surface. | The variant's own surface |
| `--badge-ink` | Badge label colour in every variant. Unset, each variant keeps its own text colour. | The variant's own text colour |

A theme-wide `bg` / `ink` binding paints every variant the same, including `destructive` and `success`, so status colour is lost. To tint one badge or one region, set `--badge-bg` / `--badge-ink` on that badge or its container instead.

### `status-badge`

Status-badge indicator dot and the mono readout label. Chrome is inherited from the Badge family.

| Token | Binds | Falls back to |
|---|---|---|
| `--status-badge-dot-size` | Indicator dot diameter. | `0.5rem` |
| `--status-badge-dot-radius` | Indicator dot rounding — square it for a Linear-style status marker. | `var(--radius-full, 9999px)` |
| `--status-badge-mono-font-family` | Mono-label family. | `var(--font-mono, "SF Mono", "Fira Code", "Fira Mono", monospace)` |
| `--status-badge-mono-font-size` | Mono-label type size. | `var(--text-11, 0.6875rem)` |
| `--status-badge-mono-letter-spacing` | Mono-label tracking. | `0.02em` |

### `filter-bar`

| Token | Binds | Falls back to |
|---|---|---|
| `--filter-bar-bg` | Filter-bar fill. | `var(--surface-card, #ffffff)` |
| `--filter-bar-border` | Filter-bar frame. | `1px solid var(--border-default, #e5e7eb)` |
| `--filter-bar-radius` | Filter-bar corner rounding. | `var(--radius-lg, 0.75rem)` |
| `--filter-bar-padding` | Filter-bar inset. | `var(--spacing-3, 0.75rem) var(--spacing-4, 1rem)` |
| `--filter-bar-gap` | Vertical rhythm between the control row and the chip row. | `var(--spacing-3, 0.75rem)` |
| `--filter-bar-text-color` | Filter-bar text colour. | `var(--text-primary, #111827)` |
| `--filter-bar-dense-padding` | Dense-variant inset. | `var(--spacing-2, 0.5rem) var(--spacing-3, 0.75rem)` |
| `--filter-bar-dense-gap` | Dense-variant rhythm. | `var(--spacing-2, 0.5rem)` |
| `--filter-bar-control-radius` | Rounding of the search input and filter triggers inside the bar. | `var(--radius-md, 0.25rem)` |
| `--filter-bar-results-font-size` | Results-count type size. | `var(--font-size-sm, 0.875rem)` |
| `--filter-bar-results-color` | Results-count colour. | `var(--text-secondary, #6b7280)` |

| `--banner-font-size` | Banner base type size. | `var(--font-size-sm, 0.875rem)` |

| `--banner-info-bg` | Info-intent fill. | `var(--surface-info-subtle, transparent)` |

| `--skeleton-line-heading-height` | Heading-line placeholder height. | `18px` |
| `--skeleton-line-body-height` | Body-line placeholder height. | `14px` |
| `--skeleton-avatar-size` | Avatar placeholder diameter. | `40px` |
| `--skeleton-avatar-lg-size` | Large avatar placeholder diameter. | `64px` |
| `--skeleton-badge-width` | Row-badge placeholder width. | `72px` |
| `--skeleton-badge-height` | Row-badge placeholder height. | `22px` |
| `--skeleton-row-gap` | Skeleton row gap. | `var(--spacing-3, 0.75rem)` |
| `--skeleton-row-padding` | Skeleton row inset. | `var(--spacing-3, 0.75rem) 0` |
| `--skeleton-row-border-bottom` | Skeleton row separator. | `1px solid var(--border-default, #e5e7eb)` |

### `checkbox`

Control sizing — the D3 Tier-2 `--checkbox-size` / `-radius` / `-bg` / `-border` set, promoted from the admin-ui audit to a bindable contract.

| Token | Binds | Falls back to |
|---|---|---|
| `--checkbox-size` | Checkbox box size. | `1rem` |
| `--checkbox-radius` | Checkbox corner rounding — square it for the editorial admin look. | `var(--radius-sm, 0.25rem)` |
| `--checkbox-bg` | Unchecked fill. | `transparent` |
| `--checkbox-border` | Unchecked edge colour. Width and style come from the shared `control` edge, so `control.edge-width: 0` turns it off. | `var(--control-edge-color, var(--border-default, #e5e7eb))` |
| `--checkbox-edgeless-bg` | Unchecked fill shown only while the shared edge is off (`control.edge-width: 0`), so the box still reads as a control. | `var(--control-edge-color, var(--border-default, #e5e7eb))` |
| `--checkbox-bg-checked` | Checked fill. | `var(--interactive-primary-bg, var(--primary, #111827))` |
| `--checkbox-border-checked` | Checked edge colour. | `var(--interactive-primary-bg, var(--primary, #111827))` |

### `input`

Input shape at the default `md` size. Each key falls back to the matching
`--input-*-md` variable, so a scope that sets one still applies while the key is
unbound; a bound key wins.

| Token | Binds | Falls back to |
|---|---|---|
| `--input-md-height` | `md` height. Unbound, the height follows the padding and the line. Bind `md-padding` with it. | `var(--input-height-md, auto)` |
| `--input-md-padding` | `md` padding. Also the padding of DialogField's medium well, so the well tracks the field. | `var(--input-padding-md, var(--spacing-3_5, 0.875rem) var(--spacing-4, 1rem))` |
| `--input-md-radius` | `md` corner rounding. Also the rounding of DialogField's well. | `var(--input-radius-md, var(--radius-sm, 0.5rem))` |

### `textarea`

Textarea shape at the default `md` size.

| Token | Binds | Falls back to |
|---|---|---|
| `--textarea-padding` | `md` padding. | `var(--spacing-3_5, 0.875rem) var(--spacing-4, 1rem)` |
| `--textarea-radius` | `md` corner rounding. | `var(--radius-sm, 0.5rem)` |

### `select`

Select trigger shape at the default `md` size.

| Token | Binds | Falls back to |
|---|---|---|
| `--select-height` | `md` trigger height. Unbound, the height follows the padding and the line. Bind `padding` with it. | `auto` |
| `--select-padding` | `md` trigger padding. | `var(--spacing-3_5, 0.875rem) var(--spacing-4, 1rem)` |

A 40px field with `10px 12px` padding and 9px corners, on all three:

```yaml
components:
  input:
    md-height: "40px"
    md-padding: "10px 12px"
    md-radius: "9px"
  textarea:
    padding: "10px 12px"
    radius: "9px"
  select:
    height: "40px"
    padding: "10px 12px"
    radius: "9px"
```

### `tag-input`

TagInput — the field around the tags, each held tag, and the opt-in typing slot
(`entryAs="slot"`). The slot follows the tag's shape unless its own keys are set.

| Token | Binds | Falls back to |
|---|---|---|
| `--tag-input-min-height` | Field minimum height. The field grows as tags wrap. | `2.25rem` |
| `--tag-input-padding` | Field padding around the tags. | `var(--spacing-1, 0.25rem) var(--spacing-2, 0.5rem)` |
| `--tag-input-radius` | Field corner rounding. | `var(--radius-md, 0.375rem)` |
| `--tag-input-tag-height` | Held-tag height. Unbound, the tag is as tall as its line. | `auto` |
| `--tag-input-tag-padding-x` | Held-tag horizontal padding. | `var(--spacing-2, 0.5rem)` |
| `--tag-input-tag-font-size` | Held-tag type size. The typing slot types at it too. | `var(--font-size-xs, 0.75rem)` |
| `--tag-input-tag-font-weight` | Held-tag weight. Unbound, the tag inherits its row's weight. | `revert-layer` |
| `--tag-input-tag-radius` | Held-tag corner rounding (a pill today). | `var(--radius-full, 9999px)` |
| `--tag-input-slot-height` | Typing-slot height. Follows `tag-height`. | `var(--tag-input-tag-height, 1.375rem)` |
| `--tag-input-slot-padding-x` | Typing-slot horizontal padding. Follows `tag-padding-x`. | `var(--tag-input-tag-padding-x, var(--spacing-2, 0.5rem))` |
| `--tag-input-slot-radius` | Typing-slot corner rounding. Follows `tag-radius`. | `var(--tag-input-tag-radius, var(--radius-full, 9999px))` |
| `--tag-input-slot-min-width` | Typing-slot minimum width. The slot grows with what is typed. | `4rem` |

The typing slot draws its dashed edge from `--control-drop-edge-width` and
`--control-drop-edge-style`, so `edges: off` turns it off with every other edge.
A 29px tag and slot with 9px corners, in a 40px field:

```yaml
components:
  tag-input:
    min-height: "40px"
    padding: "5px"
    radius: "9px"
    tag-height: "29px"
    tag-padding-x: "10px"
    tag-font-weight: "300"
    tag-radius: "9px"
```

```tsx
<TagInput entryAs="slot" defaultValue={["techno", "house"]} />
```

### `control`

The one switch for form-control edges. Every form control — Input, Textarea,
Select, Checkbox, Switch, TagInput, Chip, FileUpload, EmptyState and the edged
Button faces — draws its resting edge from these, so `edge-width: 0` removes
every resting edge at once, dashed edges included.

| Token | Binds | Falls back to |
|---|---|---|
| `--control-edge-width` | **The switch.** Resting-edge weight for every form control; `0` turns every resting edge off. | `1px` (Chip: `var(--stroke-width-thin, 1px)`) |
| `--control-edge-color` | Resting-edge colour. A component's own `--<component>-border` override still wins over it. | `var(--border-default, #e5e7eb)` |
| `--control-edge-style` | Resting-edge style for solid edges. | `solid` |
| `--control-drop-edge-width` | Dashed-edge weight (FileUpload draws it at 2×). Follows `edge-width` unless set — set it alone to keep dashed edges while solid edges are off. | `var(--control-edge-width, 1px)` |
| `--control-drop-edge-style` | Dashed-edge style for drop targets, empty states and the TagInput typing slot. | `dashed` |
| `--control-state-edge-width` | Focus and invalid edge weight. Independent of `edge-width`, so focus and invalid stay visible with edges off. | `1px` |
| `--control-invalid-ring-width` | Width of the error-colour ring on a refused value. Unbound, Input draws a 1.5px inset ring and Textarea and Select draw it at `state-edge-width`. | `1.5px` (Textarea, Select: `var(--control-state-edge-width, 1px)`) |
| `--control-invalid-halo-width` | Width of the soft error-colour halo outside the ring. Unbound, Input draws none and Textarea and Select draw it at `--focus-ring-width`. | `0px` (Textarea, Select: `var(--focus-ring-width, 2px)`) |

Turning every edge off is one line in the theme:

```yaml
# my-theme.visor.yaml
edges: off   # shorthand for components.control.edge-width: "0"
```

Or set the token on any ancestor, for one part of an app:

```css
.editor {
  --control-edge-width: 0;
}
```

How the switch holds up:

- **No layout shift.** The edge is an `outline` pulled inside the box with a
  matching negative `outline-offset`, over a transparent border that only holds
  the box's geometry. Flipping the switch moves nothing.
- **No `border` to fight.** Nothing visible depends on `border-color`, so a
  consumer never needs a `border-color: transparent !important` override.
- **Focus and invalid stay visible.** They draw at `state-edge-width`, which the
  switch does not touch.
- **The checkbox still reads as a box.** With the edge off, an unchecked
  checkbox takes a fill (`--checkbox-edgeless-bg`), because the box is the
  control, not decoration.
- **Dashed edges can come back on their own.** Set `--control-drop-edge-width`
  to keep drop-target and empty-state edges while solid edges stay off.

The refused-value look on Input, Textarea and Select is a ring in the error
colour plus a soft halo. A 1px ring with a 3px halo on all three:

```yaml
components:
  control:
    invalid-ring-width: "1px"
    invalid-halo-width: "3px"
```

### `hairline`

The one switch for hairlines. Every hairline rule, divider and ring — the soft
separators and rings coloured by `--hairline` and `--hairline-strong` — reads its
weight from `--hairline-width`, so `width: 0` removes all of them at once.
Independent of the `control` edge switch above: neither touches the other's
tokens.

| Token | Binds | Falls back to |
|---|---|---|
| `--hairline-width` | **The switch.** Hairline weight for every `--hairline` / `--hairline-strong` rule; `0` turns every hairline off. Focus and invalid edges are untouched. | `1px` (most components: `var(--stroke-width-thin, 1px)`) |

Turning every hairline off is one line in the theme:

```yaml
# my-theme.visor.yaml
hairlines: off   # shorthand for components.hairline.width: "0"
```

Or set the token on any ancestor, for one part of an app:

```css
.canvas {
  --hairline-width: 0;
}
```

How the switch holds up:

- **Independent of `edges`.** `hairlines: off` emits only `--hairline-width: 0`
  and `edges: off` emits only `--control-edge-width: 0`. Set both, either, or
  neither.
- **No layout shift.** Hairlines follow the same rule as the `control` edge:
  the box keeps its geometry and only the paint changes. A ring (all four
  sides) is an `outline` pulled inside a transparent border of constant width
  (`outline-offset: calc(-1 * var(--hairline-width))`); a single rule (a rail,
  a header or footer rule, a divider) is a transparent border of constant width
  with the line painted by `border-image` at `--hairline-width`; a divider that
  is its own 1px box is an inset `box-shadow`. Flipping the switch moves
  nothing. Rendering with it on is unchanged.
- **Two exceptions, both collapsed-border tables.** `border-image` and
  `outline` do not apply to a `border-collapse: collapse` cell, so Table's
  cell hairline and MatrixTable's header and cell rules stay real borders. Table's
  cell rule shares its edge with the row rule, so removing it moves nothing;
  MatrixTable's header/body join has no second rule, so it tightens by 1px.
- **A bound border shorthand wins.** `--tabs-line-border-bottom` and
  `--dialog-form-panel-border` take a full border value. Bound, they draw that
  border instead of the painted hairline, and the switch no longer governs them.
- **Colour is still yours.** `--hairline` and `--hairline-strong` are unchanged;
  the switch is the width, so a theme can still tune the colour while hairlines
  are on.
- **Focus and invalid stay visible.** They draw at `--control-state-edge-width`,
  which this switch does not touch.

### `switch`

Switch track and knob dimensions (default size; `size="sm"` keeps its own) and colours. Set `knob-inset` to size the knob from the track: it sits that far from the track's outer edge on every side.

| Token | Binds | Falls back to |
|---|---|---|
| `--switch-track-width` | Track width. | `2rem` |
| `--switch-track-height` | Track height. With `knob-inset` set, the knob is the track height less the inset on both sides. | `1.15rem` |
| `--switch-knob-inset` | Gap between the knob and the track's outer edge, on every side. Unset, the knob keeps its shipped 1rem size and position. | — (unset) |
| `--switch-track-bg` | Unchecked track fill. | `var(--border-default, #e5e7eb)` |
| `--switch-edge-color` | Track edge colour — transparent by default. Width and style come from the shared `control` edge, so `control.edge-width: 0` turns it off. | `transparent` |
| `--switch-track-hover-bg` | Unchecked track fill under the pointer. Bind it in a borderless theme, where `--border-strong` is transparent. | `var(--border-strong, #d1d5db)` |
| `--switch-track-hover-bg-checked` | Checked track fill under the pointer. Unbound it is `--border-strong`, as it always was; bind it to keep the checked fill under the pointer. | `var(--border-strong, #d1d5db)` |
| `--switch-knob-bg` | Unchecked knob fill. Bind it in a dark theme, where the page colour is a black knob on a dark track. | `var(--surface-page, #ffffff)` |
| `--switch-knob-bg-checked` | Checked knob fill. Independent of `knob-bg`, so a light unchecked knob can sit beside a dark knob on a bright checked track. | `var(--surface-page, #ffffff)` |

Every hook in `field`, `button`, `text` and `switch` defaults to what shipped
before it existed. Case and tracking are declared in Visor's lowest cascade
layer (`visor-base`, where the reset lives) and fall back to `revert-layer`, so
while a hook is unset the element is exactly as it would be without it: your
own rules, a utility class, a reset, inheritance or the browser's `<button>`
default still decide. Set, the hook still yields to any rule of yours.

A compact caps pill for dialog actions, a 13px state line and a caps state tag:

```yaml
# my-theme.visor.yaml
components:
  button:
    dlg-font-size: "10px"
    dlg-text-transform: uppercase
    dlg-letter-spacing: "0.06em"
    dlg-radius: "999px"
  text:
    sm-font-size: "13px"
    xs-font-size: "9px"
    xs-text-transform: uppercase
    xs-letter-spacing: "0.12em"
  field:
    label-font-size: "9px"
    label-text-transform: uppercase
    label-letter-spacing: "0.12em"
    label-color: "var(--text-tertiary)"
  switch:
    track-width: "30px"
    track-height: "17px"
    knob-inset: "3px"
```

None of these hooks draws an edge. The outline Button (at any size, `dlg`
included) and the Switch track take their edge from the `control` family, so
`control.edge-width: 0` still turns them off.

### `save-status`

SaveStatus readout — the fixed-width slot, its type, the Syncing ink and the Unsaved dot, so the readout never reflows its row.

| Token | Binds | Falls back to |
|---|---|---|
| `--save-status-width` | Slot width. Unbound, the slot is as wide as the longest label in the current font plus the retry mark, the same in every state. Bind it to pin a width; a longer label then truncates inside it. | `auto` |
| `--save-status-syncing-color` | Ink of the Syncing state (a first sync from an outside source). Unbound it reads `--text-secondary`. | `var(--text-secondary, #6b7280)` |
| `--save-status-font-size` | Readout type size. | `var(--font-size-xs, 0.75rem)` |
| `--save-status-dot-size` | Diameter of the status dot (`dot`), in every state but Unsaved. Also the Unsaved dot's, until `unsaved-dot-size` is set. The slot width does not change. | `var(--spacing-2, 0.5rem)` |
| `--save-status-unsaved-dot-size` | Diameter of the dot that draws Unsaved — the status dot while Unsaved, and the dot alone of `unsavedAs="dot"`. Follows `dot-size`. | `var(--save-status-dot-size, var(--spacing-2, 0.5rem))` |
| `--save-status-font-family` | Readout family (e.g. the theme's mono). | `revert-layer` |
| `--save-status-text-transform` | Readout casing. | `revert-layer` |
| `--save-status-letter-spacing` | Readout tracking. | `revert-layer` |

Family, case and tracking sit in `visor-base` and fall back to `revert-layer`,
like the type hooks above, so while they are unset the readout inherits from
its row and any rule of yours wins. A 78px caps mono readout:

```yaml
components:
  save-status:
    width: "78px"
    font-family: "var(--font-mono)"
    text-transform: uppercase
    letter-spacing: "0.06em"
```

With `dot`, SaveStatus draws a status dot before the label in every state, in
the state's ink. A 9px readout with a 5px dot that grows to 6px while unsaved:

```yaml
components:
  save-status:
    font-size: "9px"
    dot-size: "5px"
    unsaved-dot-size: "6px"
```

The dot's box is as wide as the larger diameter, so the label never moves.

SaveStatus draws no edge, so there is nothing for `control.edge-width` to turn off.

### `segmented-control`

SegmentedControl — the well, its corner radius, the sliding pill, the ink and the state edge on it. The resting edge is the shared `control` edge.

| Token | Binds | Falls back to |
|---|---|---|
| `--segmented-control-track-bg` | The well the pill slides in. Default is the page nudged 12% toward the ink, so it reads as a well in light and dark. | `color-mix(in srgb, var(--text-primary, #111827) 12%, var(--surface-page, #ffffff))` |
| `--segmented-control-radius` | Track corner radius. Unset, each size keeps its ToggleGroup radius. | xs `var(--radius-md, 0.375rem)`, sm and md `var(--radius-lg, 0.5rem)`, lg `var(--radius-xl, 0.75rem)` |
| `--segmented-control-indicator-bg` | Sliding active pill. Bind a lifted dark fill where the theme wants one. | `var(--interactive-primary-bg, var(--primary, #111827))` |
| `--segmented-control-indicator-text` | Active segment label ink, on the pill. | `var(--interactive-primary-text, #f9fafb)` |
| `--segmented-control-indicator-edge` | Colour of the 1px state edge on the active pill. Set `transparent` where the fill already clears 3:1 against the well. | `var(--text-primary, #111827)` |
| `--segmented-control-inactive-text` | Inactive segment label colour. | `var(--text-primary, #111827)` |
| `--segmented-control-active-weight` | Active segment label weight. | `var(--font-weight-medium, 500)` |

The state edge is an inset ring at `--control-state-edge-width` (the width focus and invalid use), so
`control.edge-width: 0` turns the resting edge off and leaves the state edge, with no layout shift. A theme
whose pill already clears 3:1 against the well, such as an accent fill on black, binds it to `transparent`:

```yaml
components:
  segmented-control:
    indicator-edge: "transparent"
```

A red pill with white ink, muted inactive labels, a bold active label and an 8px track:

```yaml
components:
  segmented-control:
    indicator-bg: "#e51a1a"
    indicator-text: "#ffffff"
    inactive-text: "rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.46)"
    active-weight: "600"
    radius: "8px"
```

SegmentedControl's resting edge is an outline from `--control-edge-*`, so
`control.edge-width: 0` turns it off while focus stays visible.

### `tooltip`

Tooltip ground and ink, so a dark theme can keep the label legible without retuning the shared inverse pair other components read.

| Token | Binds | Falls back to |
|---|---|---|
| `--tooltip-bg` | Tooltip ground. | `var(--surface-overlay, #111827)` |
| `--tooltip-text` | Tooltip label colour. | `var(--text-inverse, #ffffff)` |

Unbound, the tooltip reads `--surface-overlay` under `--text-inverse`, as it
always has. In a dark theme both can resolve dark, and `--text-inverse` cannot
be retuned for the tooltip alone: it is the dark ink Calendar, Badge and Chip
set on light and accent fills. Bind the pair in dark mode instead:

```yaml
components:
  tooltip:
    bg:
      dark: "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.8)"
    text:
      dark: "#fafafa"
```

A flat `overrides.dark.tooltip-bg` / `tooltip-text` pair emits the same two
properties through the brand pass-through.

### `action-row`

ActionRow state fills, edge and geometry: rest, hover, open, selected and disabled each read their own token.

| Token | Binds | Falls back to |
|---|---|---|
| `--action-row-min-height` | Row floor height; the whole row is the target. | `2.75rem` |
| `--action-row-padding` | Row inset, kept inside the hover and selected fills. | `var(--spacing-2, 0.5rem) var(--spacing-3, 0.75rem)` |
| `--action-row-gap` | Gap between the leading slot, the title block and the trailing slot. | `var(--spacing-3, 0.75rem)` |
| `--action-row-radius` | Row corner rounding (the hover and selected fill). | `var(--radius-md, 0.375rem)` |
| `--action-row-hover-bg` | Hover fill. | `var(--surface-interactive-hover, #f3f4f6)` |
| `--action-row-open-bg` | Fill of a row that has opened a picker or popover (`aria-expanded`). | `var(--surface-interactive-hover, #f3f4f6)` |
| `--action-row-selected-bg` | Selected fill. A lifted fill, never white. | `var(--surface-interactive-active, #e5e7eb)` |
| `--action-row-selected-edge-color` | Selected row's inset edge colour. Its width is `--control-state-edge-width`, so `edges: off` keeps it. | `var(--text-secondary, #6b7280)` |
| `--action-row-disabled-opacity` | Disabled row opacity. | `var(--opacity-50, 0.5)` |
| `--action-row-title-weight` | Title weight. | `var(--font-weight-medium, 500)` |
| `--action-row-line-color` | Second-line colour. | `var(--text-secondary, #6b7280)` |
| `--action-row-leading-color` | Leading icon colour. | `var(--text-secondary, #6b7280)` |
| `--action-row-leading-size` | Leading icon size. | `1.25rem` |
| `--action-row-trailing-color` | Trailing value or caret colour. | `var(--text-secondary, #6b7280)` |

Unbound, the selected row is `--surface-interactive-active` (a neutral lift, not the accent `--surface-selected`) with a `--text-secondary`
inset edge. The row has no resting edge, and the selected edge is a state edge
at `--control-state-edge-width`, like focus and invalid: `edges: off` leaves it
(WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1 for a state indicator). The list's hairlines between rows
read `--hairline-width` (`hairlines: off`). Focus stays visible either way. A dark theme that wants the
lifted dark fill with a light edge binds the two selected tokens:

```yaml
components:
  action-row:
    selected-bg:
      dark: "#26262b"
    selected-edge-color:
      dark: "rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.24)"
```

### `input-affix`

Input and NumberInput prefix and suffix: the gap between a fixed affix and the value, and the affix's ink.

| Token | Binds | Falls back to |
|---|---|---|
| `--input-affix-gap` | Space between a prefix or suffix and the value. | `var(--spacing-2, 0.5rem)` |
| `--input-affix-color` | Prefix and suffix ink. | `var(--text-secondary, #6b7280)` |

The affix draws no edge of its own. The well keeps its one edge from the
[`control`](#control) tokens, around the affix and the value together, so
`control.edge-width: 0` turns it off and focus and invalid stay visible.

```yaml
components:
  input-affix:
    gap: "12px"
    color:
      dark: "#a3a3a3"
```

### `separator`

The line a Separator draws, bare or on both sides of a label.

| Token | Binds | Falls back to |
|---|---|---|
| `--separator-color` | Rule colour. | `var(--border-default, #e5e7eb)` |

A borderless theme sets `border-default` to transparent, which hides the rule.
Bind `separator.color` to keep it visible without bringing structural borders back.

```yaml
components:
  separator:
    color:
      dark: "#2c2c2c"
```

### `admin-ui`

Structural roles the admin-ui pattern owns. `marquee-family` is the display face for KPI hero figures and marquee page titles — the role the admin-ui portability audit named as the one piece of ENTR brand coupling a new theme must rebind.

| Token | Binds | Falls back to |
|---|---|---|
| `--admin-ui-marquee-family` | Marquee / hero-figure display family. | `var(--font-display, var(--font-family-heading, inherit))` |

## Emit-only roles

Two entries above have no Visor component reading them. They exist so a
**generated** theme can carry the admin-ui pattern's Tier-2 treatment layer
rather than leaving it as prose in a design audit — the pattern shell
(`design-prototypes/admin-ui/tokens.css`) is the consumer. `--surface-screen` is
the deepest chrome tier (the sidebar rail); bind it to the theme's deep overlay,
never to a literal.
